senses.gloss:
paurṇamāsī-vratas
(‘vratas performed on a paurṇamī or full-मोओन् day’)
------------------------------------------
This refers to a number of vratas or religious rites performed on a paurṇamī day (full-मोओन् day).
Some of them are: Āṣāḍhapūrṇimā (June-July): This is also known as गुरु-pūrṇimā or व्यासपूर्णिमा. On this day the yatis or saṁnyāsins (Hindu मोन्क्स्) are expected to have a shave and begin their Cāturmāsyavrata, spread over four or two months. During this period they are not expected to have a shave again. (See also CĀTURMĀSYA.)
Śrāvaṇapūrṇimā (July-August): On this occasion उपाकर्म has to be performed by the followers of the Ṛgveda and the Yajurveda. See UPĀKARMA for more details.
Bhādrapadapūrṇimā (August-September): This day is sacred for the performance of nāndīmukha-śrāddha for the gratification of the पितृस् or manes. See ĀBHYUDAYIKA ŚRĀDDHA.
Pauṣapūrṇimā (December-January): By bathing the image of वासुदेव in ghee and by worshipping the gods विष्णु, इन्द्र and बृहस्पति on this day, a person attains prosperity in life.
Phālgunapūrṇimā (February-March): This being the day of the होलि festival which includes Holikādahana (burning to ashes the ogress Holikā) or Kāmadahana (burning काम or Cupid)—an occasion dear to boys—they are allowed to steal firewood for this purpose!
